Programs · Free training + mentoring

The eight-week course.

Eight weeks, taken together. Everyone starts at week 1. Nobody is behind. Training runs at 139 Millwick Dr and partner venues across the GTA.

16–29

Ages welcome. 16 and 17 with a parent or guardian’s consent.

8 weeks

One cohort, taken together. Everyone starts at week 1.

Sat 10–2

Saturdays, 10:00 AM–2:00 PM, at Faithfire and partner venues.

20 places

Free. No fees, no gear purchases, no paid upsells.

Syllabus

Hands on the gear from the first morning.

01

Cables, connectors and signal flow

Coil, tape and test every cable type we own. Follow a signal from microphone to speaker and find the break we hid in it.

02

Digital consoles: the Wing and X32

Build a show file from empty: inputs, gains, EQ, routing, scenes. The two consoles most GTA rooms actually run.

03

Mixing a live band

Soundcheck a real band at Faithfire. Vocals first, then everything else. Learn what to do when it feeds back anyway.

04

Cameras and video switching (ATEM)

Frame, focus and follow. Then sit in the director’s chair and call a two-camera rehearsal on comms.

05

Lighting: rigging safely, running a desk

Hang, focus and cable a rig without hurting anyone. Program cues and run a service from the lighting desk.

06

Streaming, lyrics and media

Build a full ProPresenter service file: lyrics, scripture, sermon slides, stream output. Advance it live, on the director’s call.

07

Show calling, comms and event etiquette

Call a show start to finish. Comms discipline, dress codes, client manners — the conduct half of the job.

08

Capstone: crew a real production

A full event, crewed entirely by the cohort, mentors on comms only if needed. This is the reference you graduate with.

After the course

Pathways, not promises.

We don’t promise jobs. We promise hours on real gear, a reference, and a crew that will say your name when a call comes in.

Mentoring

One-to-one, with a working technician.

Monthly check-ins. All mentors are police-checked and meet participants in crew spaces, never alone off-site.

Pathway · Production management

Run the whole show.

Advancing the event, building the run sheet and call sheets, managing the budget, and calling the show on the day.

Pathway · Technical management

Lead the department.

Planning the rig, choosing and maintaining the gear, signing off on safety, and teaching the next cohort.

Safeguarding · Our standards

  • Every mentor passes a Vulnerable Sector Check before working with participants and follows a written code of conduct.
  • Mentors and participants meet in crew spaces, never alone off-site.
  • Participants aged 16 and 17 join with a parent or guardian’s consent.
  • Photos and recordings of participants are used only with consent, which can be withdrawn at any time.
  • The program is free, and it stays free. No fees, no gear purchases, no paid upsells.

Come as you are. Leave with a trade.

January cohort · Twenty places · Saturdays 10:00 AM–2:00 PM

Apply nowDonate

An eight-week course, Saturdays 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM, at Faithfire Production, 139 Millwick Dr, and partner venues across the GTA. Cables and signal flow in week 1; a full production crewed by the cohort in week 8.

Every participant is paired with a working technician: someone who mixed, switched or lit a show this month. Monthly check-ins at minimum, help with first bookings, rates, and when to say no.

First bookings are usually cable and stagehand calls, then operating positions. We don't promise you a job. We promise hands-on time with real gear, honest instruction, a reference from people the industry knows, and a crew that'll say your name when a call comes in.

The other half of putting on a show: advancing the event, building the run sheet and call sheets, managing the budget, and calling the show on the day. Participants who work well on a crew learn to run the production, not just handle one role in it.

For those who go on to lead a department: planning the rig, choosing and maintaining the gear, signing off on safety, and teaching the next cohort. It's the top of the pathway, the people who spec out the room and are accountable for it.

Build a full service file: lyrics, scripture, sermon slides, stream output. Advance it live, on the director's call.
